name: Filesystem MCP Server
description: Lets Claude read, write, search and organise files inside folders you explicitly allow. Handy for working through a folder of notes, essays or lesson plans.
author: Model Context Protocol maintainers
install:
1. Pick the folders Claude may touch (it cannot leave them).
2. Add the config below to your MCP client's config file, replacing the paths.
3. Restart the client; the file tools should appear.
4. On Windows the README launches npx through cmd /c.
use_cases: Summarise a folder of lecture notes
Rename and sort downloaded study material
Draft files directly into a project folder
Read a student essay folder for feedback
example_prompts: List every markdown file in my notes folder and group them by topic.
Read essay1.txt and give feedback on structure.

name: Fetch MCP Server
description: Gives Claude a way to download a web page and convert it to clean text, so it can read articles, docs and reference pages you point it at.
author: Model Context Protocol maintainers
install:
1. Install uv (the README uses uvx), or use the pip or docker variants it lists.
2. Add the config below to your MCP client.
3. Restart the client and ask Claude to open a URL.
use_cases: Summarise a news article or paper page
Pull a documentation page into a study guide
Compare two web sources on one topic
Check a cited link actually says what is claimed
example_prompts: Fetch this URL and give me a 5-bullet summary.
Read this page and make 10 quiz questions from it.

name: Memory MCP Server
description: A knowledge-graph style memory that lets Claude remember people, topics and facts across chats. Useful for long courses or ongoing research.
author: Model Context Protocol maintainers
install:
1. Add the npx config below to your MCP client (a docker variant also exists in the README).
2. Restart the client.
3. Tell Claude what to remember; it stores entities and relations locally.
use_cases: Remember a student's weak topics across sessions
Build a concept map as a course progresses
Track reading list and key authors
example_prompts: Remember that my exam is on chemistry bonding next Friday.
What topics have I said I find hard so far?

name: Sequential Thinking MCP Server
description: Provides a tool for working through a problem in numbered, revisable steps. Good for maths proofs, planning essays and debugging reasoning.
author: Model Context Protocol maintainers
install:
1. Add the npx config below to your MCP client.
2. Restart the client.
3. Ask Claude to think a problem through step by step using the tool.
use_cases: Work through a multi-step maths problem
Plan an essay outline and revise it
Show reasoning steps for a lesson
example_prompts: Use sequential thinking to plan my 2000-word essay on climate policy.
Solve this physics problem step by step and revisit any weak step.

name: Git MCP Server
description: Lets Claude inspect and work with a local Git repository: status, diffs, logs and commits. Suits coding classes and student project reviews.
author: Model Context Protocol maintainers
install:
1. Install uv (README uses uvx) or use its pip/docker options.
2. Add the config below, pointing --repository at your repo.
3. Restart the client and ask about the repo history.
use_cases: Explain what changed between two commits
Teach Git by walking through a repo
example_prompts: Show the last 5 commits and summarise them.
What files changed in the latest commit?

name: Time MCP Server
description: Adds current-time and timezone conversion tools so Claude stops guessing dates. Useful for scheduling classes and study timetables across regions.
author: Model Context Protocol maintainers
install:
1. Install uv (README uses uvx) or use pip/docker variants.
2. Add the config below to your MCP client.
3. Restart and ask for a time conversion.
use_cases: Plan a revision schedule with real dates
example_prompts: What time is 9am IST in London and New York?
How many days until 15 March?

name: Notion MCP Server (self-hosted)
description: Connects Claude to a Notion workspace through the Notion API so it can search and edit pages and databases. The repo now recommends Notion's hosted remote MCP instead.
author: Notion
install:
1. Note: the README says this local server is no longer actively maintained and points to Notion's hosted Remote MCP (developers.notion.com/docs/mcp) as preferred.
2. For the local one, create a Notion integration token and share pages with it.
3. Add the config below to your MCP client, replacing the token.
4. Restart the client.
use_cases: Search class notes stored in Notion
example_prompts: Find my notes page on photosynthesis and summarise it.
Add a new row to my assignments database.

name: GitHub MCP Server
description: GitHub's official server for reading repositories, issues and pull requests from an AI assistant. Fits coding courses and open-source learning.
author: GitHub
install:
1. Docker is needed to run the local server image ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server (the README also has a hosted option).
2. Create a GitHub personal access token with only the permissions you are comfortable granting.
3. Claude Code command from the README: claude mcp add github -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=$GITHUB_PAT -- docker run -i --rm -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server
4. Or put the config below in your client config.
use_cases: Triage issues in a class project repo
Summarise a pull request for review
example_prompts: List open issues labelled 'good first issue' in my repo.
Summarise the latest pull request.

name: Playwright MCP Server
description: Microsoft's browser-automation server: Claude can open pages, click, fill forms and read page structure. Great for teaching web testing or scripted research.
author: Microsoft
install:
1. Needs Node.js.
2. Claude Code command from the README: claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest
3. Or add the config below to any MCP client and restart.
use_cases: Walk through a website to document steps
example_prompts: Open example.com and describe the page structure.
Test the signup form on my local site.

name: Context7 MCP Server
description: Fetches current, version-specific library documentation so coding answers rely on up-to-date docs rather than old training data. Useful for programming students.
author: Upstash
install:
1. The README quick setup is: npx ctx7 setup (needs a recent Node.js; it handles login and offers skill or MCP mode).
2. Manual option: point your MCP client at https://mcp.context7.com/mcp with an Authorization: Bearer header using your API key.
3. In prompts, add 'use context7' to trigger it.
use_cases: Learn a framework from its latest docs
Avoid outdated code examples in assignments
Look up library usage while coding
example_prompts: Show how to set up routing in Next.js. use context7
Explain pandas groupby using current docs. use context7

name: Brave Search MCP Server
description: Brave's official server giving Claude web, news, image and local search through the Brave Search API. Good for research tasks that need fresh sources.
author: Brave
install:
1. Get a Brave Search API key.
2. Add the npx config below to your MCP client, replacing the key.
3. Restart and ask Claude to search the web.
use_cases: Find recent sources for a research paper
Check current news on a topic
Find local libraries or study spots
example_prompts: Search for recent studies on spaced repetition and list 5 sources.
What is the latest news on the topic of my essay?

name: Everything MCP Test Server
description: A reference server that exposes prompts, resources and tools in one place. Meant for learning how MCP works and testing clients, not for daily use.
author: Model Context Protocol maintainers
install:
1. Read src/everything in the servers repo for current run instructions (it is the one reference server that also supports Streamable HTTP).
2. Register it in your MCP client like the other servers, then inspect which tools, prompts and resources appear.
3. Use it to teach or learn how MCP clients behave.
use_cases: Teach students what MCP tools/resources/prompts are
Demo an MCP connection in class
example_prompts: List the tools the everything server provides.
Call the echo tool with 'hello'.

name: Claude Plugins Official Marketplace
description: Anthropic's official plugin marketplace for Claude Code, holding its own plugins and some legacy third-party ones. The easiest starting point for adding plugins.
author: Anthropic
install:
1. Inside Claude Code run: /plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official
2. Or open /plugin and use the Discover tab.
3. Only install plugins you trust; the README warns plugins can bundle MCP servers and other software.
use_cases: See the standard plugin folder layout
Learn how plugins bundle commands, agents and MCP
example_prompts: Show me how to install a plugin from the official marketplace.
What does a plugin folder contain?

name: Claude Code Plugins Directory
description: The plugins folder inside the Claude Code repository, explaining plugin structure and a marketplace that points to Anthropic-built plugins. Good for learning the format.
author: Anthropic
install:
1. Install Claude Code using the README method for your OS.
2. Run claude in your project, then use /plugin to install from marketplaces.
3. Read plugins/README.md in the repo for the plugin layout (plugin.json, commands, agents, skills, hooks, .mcp.json).
example_prompts: Explain each folder in a Claude Code plugin.
How do I add a marketplace?

name: Anthropic Agent Skills Marketplace
description: Anthropic's example skills repo, usable as a Claude Code marketplace. Includes document skills (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx) and example skills for creative and technical work.
author: Anthropic
install:
1. In Claude Code run: /plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills
2. Install a set: /plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills (or example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills)
3. Then just mention the task, e.g. use the PDF skill.
4. The README says these are demonstration and educational examples; test before relying on them.
use_cases: Start your own skill from the template
example_prompts: Use the PDF skill to extract the form fields from this file.
Make a slide deck from my lesson outline.

name: Knowledge Work Plugins
description: Role-based plugin collection from Anthropic for Cowork and Claude Code, bundling skills, commands and connectors for jobs like productivity, data, enterprise search and bio-research.
author: Anthropic
install:
1. In Claude Code run: claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins
2. Then install one, e.g.: claude plugin install sales@knowledge-work-plugins (swap in the plugin you want, such as productivity or data)
3. In Cowork, install from claude.com/plugins instead.
use_cases: Write and check SQL for data classes
Customise plugins for a school or team
example_prompts: Use the productivity plugin to plan my week.
Help me write a SQL query for this dataset.

name: Life Sciences Marketplace
description: Anthropic marketplace of research skills for life sciences, such as clinical protocol drafting and structured scientific problem selection. Handy for science students and researchers.
author: Anthropic
install:
1. In Claude Code run: /plugin marketplace add anthropics/life-sciences
2. Install a skill, e.g.: /plugin install scientific-problem-selection@life-sciences
3. Others listed in the README include clinical-trial-protocol and binder-gauntlet.
use_cases: Choose and refine a research question
Plan next steps on a stuck project
example_prompts: Help me pick between two thesis topics.
Pressure-test my research idea.

name: Superpowers
description: A software-development methodology packaged as skills: brainstorming a spec, planning, test-first work and review. Teaches disciplined habits to coding learners.
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
install:
1. In Claude Code run: /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
2. Alternatively: /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace then /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
3. Start a build task and Claude will begin by asking what you want to achieve.
use_cases: Plan small projects step by step
example_prompts: Help me build a to-do app; start with the design.
Plan this feature before writing code.

name: Superpowers Marketplace
description: A small curated Claude Code marketplace from the Superpowers author, listing Superpowers and related workflow plugins.
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
install:
1. In Claude Code run: /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
2. Then: /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
3. Check its README for the other plugins listed.
use_cases: Learn how marketplaces are laid out
example_prompts: What plugins does this marketplace offer?
Install the core skills library.

name: Agents, Skills and Plugins Collection
description: A large open collection of Claude Code plugins covering Python, JavaScript, testing, security and more, installed via a marketplace.
author: Seth Hobson (wshobson)
install:
1. In Claude Code run: /plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents
2. Then: /plugin install python-development@claude-code-workflows
3. Try the plugin's command, e.g. /python-development:python-scaffold Create a FastAPI service with tests
example_prompts: Scaffold a FastAPI service with tests.
Review this function for bugs.

name: Claude Code Templates
description: A big browsable catalog (aitmpl.com) of skills, agents, commands, hooks and MCP servers with a CLI that installs chosen components into your project.
author: Daniel Avila (davila7)
install:
1. The README says it runs with npx, no global install: npx claude-code-templates@latest
2. Install one item, e.g.: npx claude-code-templates@latest --agent development-tools/code-reviewer
3. Search from terminal: npx claude-code-templates@latest --search "code review"
example_prompts: Search the catalog for a code review agent.
Install a frontend design skill.

name: Awesome Claude Code
description: A hand-curated list of Claude Code resources: guides, skills, agents, status lines, tools and plugins. Includes learning guides, good for self-study.
author: hesreallyhim and contributors
install:
1. This is a reading list, not a plugin to install.
2. Browse the README sections and open linked projects you like.
3. Follow each linked project's own install steps.
example_prompts: Which resources in this list help beginners learn Claude Code?
Find hooks examples.

name: Awesome Claude Plugins (Composio)
description: A curated list of Claude Code plugins from Composio, featuring a connect-apps plugin that lets Claude act in many external apps via Composio.
author: ComposioHQ
install:
1. Clone the repo: git clone https://github.com/composiohq/awesome-claude-plugins.git then cd awesome-claude-plugins
2. Load a plugin locally: claude --plugin-dir ./connect-apps
3. Run its setup command inside Claude and paste your Composio API key when asked.
use_cases: Connect Claude to email or issue trackers
Try a plugin from a local folder
example_prompts: Run the connect-apps setup.
What plugins are listed for productivity?
